Optimize the current consuming website for its declared SEO goals. Read its `AGENTS.md` and context, then apply `seo-optimization` in full. The website's purpose, audience, content, constraints and evidence determine the approach.

Compare useful proposals. Explain what each gains, what it costs and why you recommend it. If only one reasonable path exists, explain it and proceed within existing authorization. If several viable strategies remain, present the options and recommendations, ask the user to choose and wait before implementing dependent work. Routine fixes within a selected path do not require repeated approval. Include opportunities beyond fixing audit failures. For a new website, work from its declared requirements and available implementation. Do not require historical analytics before producing a provisional plan.

Use audit evidence when it helps the decision. Keep missing measurements explicit. Preserve the read-only boundaries of technical and off-page specialists and hand implementation to the appropriate project owner. Complete authorized work and verify it. If the request is proposal-only, deliver a reviewable recommendation without applying it.

Output the objective, evidence and assumptions, meaningful alternatives, recommended paths with reasons and the user’s selection when needed, implementation or handoff, validation and follow-up criteria. Keep project-specific plans and data in the consuming project. Do not invent performance or search forecasts or guarantee rankings.

## Checklist assessment

When reporting a score, use the kit's scoring version and retain measured coverage, checklist bounds, category/page scope, missing evidence and critical failures. NEVER: describe the score as a Google metric or a ranking forecast. Use `seo-onpage-checklist/CONTENT_REVIEW.md` for per-page content reviews and the applicable blog, guide, review, landing or product tasks. GEO and off-page evidence require itemized review under the kit's scoring contract. A summary approval does not pass unreviewed items or pages. Do not compare numerical scores across incompatible rubrics or measurement sets. Keep N/A reasons and reviewed judgments explicit.

## Current evidence

Recheck current Google documentation for recommendations that depend on feature availability, eligibility or an update. Record dates and scope, reconcile newer explicit guidance with older references, and keep project observations separate from hypotheses. Use `seo-optimization/KNOWLEDGE.md` for update analysis when relevant. Do not treat a documentation revision as an algorithm rollout or claim access to reports absent from the actual binding. For AI visibility, keep effective Search Console inclusion, generative impressions and sampled answer observations distinct. Do not change account settings during a read-only review.

## Save deliverables

Work in the dedicated project folder selected for this website or client. Keep its context and deliverables together. When switching clients, resolve the new target folder before using context or saving files. Ask for the target if it is unclear.

Use `keyword-research/` for keyword research, `audits/` for audit evidence, `proposals/<type>/` for proposals and implementation plans, and `reports/DD/MM/YYYY/` for standalone progress reports.

Find the selected client or website folder in the active workspace and declared context. An SEO working folder without code or Git is valid. Ask for the root if it is unclear. Create only the directories you need and pass absolute paths, even when running commands from the kit checkout. Resolve paths, including symlinks, and keep destinations inside that project and outside the kit. Preserve earlier results with dated files or separate run folders. Summarize the result in chat and return the saved paths. Saving audit files does not authorize changes to website source or configuration.

Group proposals by type, such as `proposals/articles/`, `proposals/guides/`, `proposals/landings/`, `proposals/technical/` or `proposals/strategy/`. Keep decisions and implementation tracking with the corresponding proposal. Link related proposals instead of duplicating them.

Name report folders by creation date, with zero-padded day/month/year directories: `reports/19/10/2026/search-performance/`. Use the project's timezone, or UTC, and record it. Record the data period separately. Give repeated reports on the same day distinct names.
